chapter_theme: The eleventh station seen as a state (பதினோராம் தானமும் அவத்தையெனக் காணல்): counted centres in the body yield nectar, bliss and Om, and the eleven stations are themselves states of the soul; held firmly, they leave nothing but Nandi.

2299.reading: In the fifth there is nectar, in the seventh bliss, in the ninth Om, and in the eleventh, if one sets it and holds it there by craft, it becomes the body: listen, you with lips red as kinchuka flowers and the speech of a parrot.
2299.nuance: The numbers are taken as stations or centres in the yogic body, which the verse does not name. முஞ்சில் is obscure, and வஞ்சகமே நின்று (standing by guile, or by craft) and காயமாம் (becomes the body, or becomes firm) are uncertain. The addressee is a woman, often taken as Shakti.

2300.reading: The mind joined with purusha, the formless with the six, turiya beyond, and the eight that abound in spreading deep sleep: these are the rare eleven states.
2300.nuance: The verse names the eleven stations as states, but how its items add up to eleven is not clear from the text.

2301.reading: When the eleven that are shown come together and one fixes and presses the body down, there is nothing but Nandi; think on that rule which does not waver: what it gathers is firmness, and thought becomes possible.
2301.nuance: உடல் நாட்டி அழுத்திடின் (fixing and pressing the body) sounds like a yogic posture or lock. The last line is loose; ஈட்டும் அது திடம் may mean the practice gains steadiness.

source_issues: 2299: line 4 reads கிஞ்சுகக் செவ்வாய், a misprint for கிஞ்சுகச் செவ்வாய்.
